BLOCKER: `content_policy` declares `engineering/design/**` MD "generated-only" and subject to generator-output comparison, but design MDs are hand-authored (this item's own design is authored prose). Enforcing generator-authority there would fail every existing design with DERIVED_DOC_STALE; authority must be scoped to genuinely derived artifacts (BACKLOG-SUMMARY, documentation-index) only.
MAJOR: Grandfather expiry `2026-11-01` is a hard wall-clock cutoff with no named enforcement owner, gate check, or alert lead-time. Without an on-run check (e.g., warn N days before, fail after), legacy `MATERIAL_CHANGE` approvals persist silently if gates are not exercised near the date.

`DESIGN_PACK_CONFIG` appears in the observability contract but is absent from `failure_matrix` and `test_matrix`; prior Gate 1.5 MINOR (pin error codes by test) has not been demonstrably closed for this code.

Item-level `rollback` still says only "Revert the change" while `design_pack.rollback` is the full ordered sequence (revert → regenerate docs → re-run gates); the short form remains the authoritative field, recurring the prior MINOR.

`scope_owner` names `REVIEW_EXCLUDES` as the single path set, but no invariant/test asserts that `architect_review_check` ancestry coverage and `review_budget` consume the identical set from `excluded_content_check`; divergence would silently weaken coverage (recurring MAJOR class).
MINOR: `performance_bound`'s 20MB/file cap has no defined behavior on exceedance (skip vs fail vs truncate) — an undefined edge in the freshness gate.
`generator_determinism` specifies timestamp normalization and sorting but not locale/timezone pinning or tie-break ordering for equal keys; render could still diverge across environments.
No dry-run/report mode specified for derived-doc regeneration before commit, weakening blast-radius review of doc-only churn.

`review_scope` lists `config/architect-review-baseline.json` and `config/id-blocks.json` but no invariant states how baseline changes interact with ancestry checks (baseline bump invalidating evidence is unspecified).
NIT: `requirements` still contains the process note "One 2.5 on the hardening candidate; precheck passes" — recurring prior NIT; belongs in `acceptance_evidence`.
SUMMARY: Design is largely sound: Gate 1.5 findings embedded and actioned, migration cutoff pinned to UTC+SHA, single content-class owner named, language rule (tooling Python) respected, observability codes enumerated.

Top risks: the "design MD generated-only" content policy is self-contradictory and would brick all authored designs; the grandfather expiry lacks an enforcement/alert mechanism; and two recurring classes (error-code test pinning, single path-set assertion) are claimed but not demonstrably test-backed.

rereview_reason: generator authority + pinned cutoff/expiry; HIL material
